title: Use the plane keyword cues when routing an acceptance to a test-layer plane

facts.note: Primary trigger: any act of selecting, assigning, reviewing or re-checking the test-layer plane of an acceptance, regardless of artifact format, phase or whether anything changed. Recognising that routing is happening is a judgment call.

values: acceptance wording contains a plane keyword cue
facts.note: Whether the wording semantically matches a cue (and how overlapping cues such as 'token' resolve) is a judgment call; a plain keyword scan is only a hint.
Optional discovery signal only; not a required gate.
Optional discovery signal only (diff-level observer); routing an unchanged acceptance also fires.

fires: A new acceptance is written and its test-layer plane must be selected.
The plane of an existing, unchanged acceptance is reviewed or re-checked, in any artifact type.
An acceptance whose wording contains cue words such as 'render', 'timeout', 'transaction' or 'permission' is being assigned a plane.
doesNotFire: Work that neither selects nor reviews the test-layer plane of any acceptance (e.g. implementing production code, editing text with no acceptances).

given: An acceptance whose test-layer plane is being selected or reviewed
when: routing the acceptance to a test-layer plane
then: Use the plane keyword cues in the acceptance wording when selecting its plane.
prefer: Read the acceptance wording against the keyword -> plane cue table: ui: display, visible, screen, render, animation | ux: understand, clarity, steps, easy, confusing | be: validate, apply, compute, reconcile, rule | nw: request, response, timeout, websocket, stream | db: query, index, transaction, lock, row | st: asset, download, upload, cache, blob, cdn | tm: event, metrics, trace, ingest, drop | sc: schema, contract, version, field, json | au: login, token, permission, rate-limit, 403 | fn: price, balance, payout, token | if: cpu, memory, pod, node, gpu.
avoid: Selecting an acceptance's plane without consulting the keyword cues in its wording.
why: The source provides these keyword cues as the reference for selecting the test-layer plane when routing an acceptance.
evidence: For each routed acceptance, a reviewer can read the selected plane against the cue words in its wording and see that the cue table was consulted.
verifier_detail: Routing table term plane_keywords ('keyword -> plane routing table.'): ui=[display, visible, screen, render, animation]; ux=[understand, clarity, steps, easy, confusing]; be=[validate, apply, compute, reconcile, rule]; nw=[request, response, timeout, websocket, stream]; db=[query, index, transaction, lock, row]; st=[asset, download, upload, cache, blob, cdn]; tm=[event, metrics, trace, ingest, drop]; sc=[schema, contract, version, field, json]; au=[login, token, permission, rate-limit, '403']; fn=[price, balance, payout, token]; if=[cpu, memory, pod, node, gpu].
'token' appears in both au and fn; a match on 'token' alone does not by itself distinguish those planes.
'403' is a string keyword (quoted in source), not a number.
The source presents these as cues, not an exhaustive or deterministic routing algorithm.
